analysis:
Examined three changed files.

1) ToolConstraintSchema.swift (head 155-187): compileResponseSchema now calls requireExplicitResponseTypes after compilation. This is a stricter fail-closed check: response_format schemas with untyped nodes (no type/properties/additionalProperties/items/enum/const) are rejected as unsupported, so an accept-anything schema is not silently narrowed to a string grammar. It only adds rejections and does not widen acceptance. Recursion covers only properties and items, and runs after compileSchema has already bounded depth (maxDepth 16) and property count, so there is no unbounded recursion. One minor gap: raw sub-nodes under keys the compiler already rejects are not reachable. Not a security regression. Tool-argument schemas (compile) are unchanged, so forced tool_choice behavior is the same.

2) ProviderLogger.swift: adds the fixed case glmWiredLimitNotice to the closed ProviderOperationalMessage vocabulary (head 172-173). The text is a constant with only the {cli} substitution from BuildEnvironment, with no associated values or request-derived data. It preserves the public-log closed-vocabulary contract and exposes no prompt, model-ID or identifier data (A-001). The model name 'GLM-5.3-Flash' is a static string. Callers are not in the supplied units.

3) ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift: the new MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError case .unsupportedOutputControl is mapped to .clientError reason, .invalidRequest code and HTTP 400 in all three switches (head 65, 161-162, 262). It is classified as a deterministic client fault, so it is not a retry or health signal. Because the switches are exhaustive, there is no fall-through to 500. The mapper does not carry the error's associated string onto the wire, so no raw detail leaks. The enum case itself is defined in an external package (MLXLMServer) not supplied; I could not verify its payload or that the sources of the throw are sanitized. This is an unverified contract, but the mapping layer sanitizes either way.

No threat-model regressions were identified. Integration questions: where unsupportedOutputControl is thrown, and whether the response_format callers handle the new unsupported errors without partially falling back to unconstrained output.
